# Chip

`Chip` presents compact filter, category, and removable selection values. Use it when the item can be selected or dismissed; use `Badge` for passive metadata.

- **Import:** `import { Chip, ChipGroup } from "@kozmos-ds/react";`
- **Group:** Core
- **Platforms:** React, SwiftUI and Compose; linked to its Figma component through Code Connect.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/data-display-chip--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import {
  Utensils as Coffee,
  MarkerPin01 as MapPin,
  ShoppingBag01 as ShoppingBag,
  Utensils,
} from "@kozmos-ds/icons";
import { Chip, ChipGroup, ThemeProvider } from "@kozmos-ds/react";

const FilterDemo = () => {
  const [active, setActive] = useState<string>("all");
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(true);

  return (
    <ChipGroup className="max-w-[460px]">
      <Chip selected={active === "all"} onClick={() => setActive("all")}>
        All
      </Chip>
      <Chip
        icon={<Utensils />}
        selected={active === "food"}
        onClick={() => setActive("food")}
      >
        Food & Drink
      </Chip>
      <Chip
        icon={<Coffee />}
        selected={active === "coffee"}
        onClick={() => setActive("coffee")}
      >
        Coffee
      </Chip>
      <Chip
        icon={<ShoppingBag />}
        selected={active === "shopping"}
        onClick={() => setActive("shopping")}
      >
        Retail
      </Chip>
      <Chip
        icon={<MapPin />}
        selected={active === "places"}
        onClick={() => setActive("places")}
      >
        Places
      </Chip>
      {visible ? (
        <Chip onRemove={() => setVisible(false)} variant="brand">
          Open now
        </Chip>
      ) : null}
    </ChipGroup>
  );
};

export function ChipExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <FilterDemo />
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Chip

It forwards its ref to `HTMLSpanElement`. Its props are `ChipProps`, which extends `Omit<React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, "onSelect">, VariantProps<typeof chipVariants>`.

- `active`: `boolean`, optional.
- `disabled`: `boolean`, optional, default `false`.
- `icon`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.
- `onRemove`: `() => void`, optional.
- `removeLabel`: `string`, optional.
- `selected`: `boolean`, optional.
- `value`: `string`, optional.

  In a single-choice `ChipGroup`, what choosing this chip picks. The group
  then decides whether it is selected, so `selected` and `active` are not
  read, and a chip that is one of a choice offers no remove control — a
  second stop inside a radio group is not one the arrow keys can reach.

- `size`: `"sm" | "lg" | "default" | null`, optional, default `"default"`.
- `variant`: `"destructive" | "neutral" | "brand" | null`, optional, default `"neutral"`.
- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

## ChipGroup

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `ChipGroupProps`, which extends `Omit<React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "defaultValue" | "dir">`.

- `selectionMode`: `"multiple" | "single"`, optional, default `"multiple"`.

  `multiple`, the default: each chip is its own toggle, as it always was.
  `single`: the chips are one choice — a radio group, with one Tab stop and
  the arrow keys moving the choice — for a one-of-several such as "Whole
  airport / Terminal 2" (row 37). Give each chip a `value`, and the group
  an `aria-label` that names the choice.

- `value`: `string`, optional.

  The chosen chip's value, with `selectionMode="single"`: controlled.

- `defaultValue`: `string`, optional.

  The chip chosen at first, when the group holds its own choice.

- `onValueChange`: `(value: string) => void`, optional.

  Called with the chosen chip's value. A choice cannot be emptied.

- `dir`: `"ltr" | "rtl"`, optional.

  Reading direction for the arrow keys; the ThemeProvider's otherwise.

- `children`: `ReactNode`, optional.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).

    props?:

          variant?: "destructive" | "neutral" | "brand" | null | undefined;
          size?: "sm" | "lg" | "default" | null | undefined;
        } & ClassProp)
      | undefined,
  ) => string;
